A.strongest_route: component-load ODE with external open validation trace
A.data_risk: multiple external parameter sources and unit reconciliation
A.validation_route: time-to-empty holdout scenarios and conservation checks
A.rejection_condition: cannot source an open trace or justify parameter units

B.strongest_route: hybrid capacity allocation plus reliability simulation
B.fatal_risk: unsupported 2050 cost/emissions assumptions drive the recommendation
B.data_risk: critical cost, throughput, water, and emissions inputs are external
B.validation_route: mass conservation, small exact cases, scenario stress tests
B.expected_bottleneck: credible parameter sourcing rather than computation
B.rejection_condition: headline ranking reverses across plausible unsourced parameters

C.fallback_route: uniform shares with minimum constraint adjustment
C.fatal_risk: claiming latent fan votes are uniquely identified
C.data_risk: structural zeros and irregular elimination weeks
C.validation_route: elimination compatibility, held-out seasons, sensitivity across feasible votes
C.expected_bottleneck: roster reconstruction and honest uncertainty language
C.rejection_condition: active rosters cannot be reconstructed reliably from supplied fields

red_team.A: Mechanistic elegance is attractive, but missing observed traces can make validation mostly plausibility-based.
red_team.B: Transparent optimization is possible, but speculative inputs can dominate every answer.
red_team.C: The supplied data are strong, but the central votes are latent and only partially identifiable.

selection_reason: C offers the only complete official dataset, a reproducible baseline, multiple falsifiable candidate routes, direct counterfactual validation, and a coherent evidence-rich paper while explicitly accommodating partial identification.
switch_condition: Switch to A if active rosters or elimination constraints cannot be reconstructed for at least 90% of evaluable weeks; do not switch merely because latent-vote uncertainty is wide.
